labels.description: A new sentence discloses that market-driven changes such as equity market declines can reduce client demand for margin lending, described as a significant source of net interest revenue.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a new exposure (dependence of net interest revenue on margin lending demand) is disclosed; the rest of the section is unchanged.

labels.description: The Company is now said to have extensively utilized higher-cost funding sources (prior: utilized higher-cost supplemental funding sources), and 'we rely heavily on client cash balances to generate revenue' becomes 'client cash balances are a significant funding source for the generation of the Company's revenue'.
labels.rationale: criterion 3: adding 'extensively' escalates the characterization of the realized reliance on higher-cost funding and dropping 'supplemental' changes how that funding is characterized, so the rewording is not identical in meaning; the other edits ('For example', 'support' for 'facilitate') are stylistic.

labels.description: Margin loans and PALs are added to the interest-earning assets exposed to rate declines (prior: investment securities and mortgages), bank deposit account fee revenue is no longer described as earned 'primarily' under the 2023 IDA agreement, and market conditions are dropped as a driver of higher deposit rates.
labels.rationale: criteria 1 and 3: margin loans and PALs are newly disclosed as rate-sensitive assets and the 'primarily' qualifier and the market-conditions driver are removed; the unrealized-loss confidence sentence and the IDA commitments paragraph visible only in the current excerpt also appear in the full prior filing, so their absence from the prior excerpt is a page-break cut, not a change.

labels.description: Further FDIC premium increases or special assessments are now tied to potential future bank failures or similar events rather than only to the cost of resolving the 2023 bank failures, and custody is added to the relationships that interconnect financial institutions.
labels.rationale: criterion 3: the scope of the FDIC assessment risk widens to future bank failures and the interconnection channels widen to include custody; the heading rewording ('direct adverse effects') is largely stylistic.

labels.description: The current version states that margin lending activity has significantly increased in recent years due to market-driven factors and overall business growth, text the prior excerpt cuts off at a page break but which the full prior filing attributed to the Ameritrade acquisition and market-driven factors.
labels.rationale: criterion 2: the Ameritrade acquisition is dropped as the named driver of margin lending growth (and in the full filings the named FHLB advance, repurchase and brokered CD supplemental funding sources and the FHLB tangible capital condition are removed); within the overlapping excerpt text the only edit is stylistic, while the lending, margin-growth and clearing house text appears only in the current excerpt.

labels.description: The current version adds to the opening paragraph that data exposure may result from a failure to adequately destroy data during system or asset decommissioning, and shortens 'non-technical means, for example, employee misconduct' to 'employee misconduct'.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a data-exposure risk appears that the prior excerpt lacks; in the full filings this sentence was relocated from the prior's external fraud paragraph, which is removed from this risk factor now that fraud has its own risk factor (itself a removed disclosure), and the ransom sentence visible only in the current excerpt is a page-break cut in the prior excerpt.

labels.description: The current excerpt keeps only the opening two sentences, so the prior's discussion of system vulnerabilities, the 2024 cloud and third-party outages, extraordinary trading volumes, dependence on intermediaries, COVID-19 staffing and fraud prevention is absent.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: previously disclosed risks are absent from the current text; most of that gap is a page-break extraction loss, but in the full filings the fraud paragraph is genuinely removed (moved to the new fraud risk factor) and custodians are added to the intermediaries relied on, so the section is material on either reading.

labels.description: The current excerpt ends mid-sentence in the list of credit exposures, so the prior's paragraph on margin, options and futures default risk and its growth from the Ameritrade acquisition is absent.
labels.rationale: criteria 1 and 2: on the excerpts a disclosed risk is absent from the current text, and in the full filings the Ameritrade acquisition is replaced as the named driver of margin, options and futures growth by market-driven factors, overall business growth and trader client base growth; the overlapping text is identical.

labels.description: Covers reliance on external service providers for key technology, cloud infrastructure, processing, servicing, support and custody functions (combined in the heading with financial intermediaries) and the losses, reputational harm and client harm if they fail or interrupt service.

Covered reliance on external service providers for technology, cloud infrastructure, processing, servicing and support functions, the losses and disruption from their failure or service interruption, recent third-party outages, lost services during COVID-19, and the cost of switching providers.

Covers rising fraud and financial crime risk from external actors (credential theft, social engineering, AI-enabled impersonation, unauthorized transfers and account openings), deliberately fraudulent clients and insider employee misconduct, plus losses reimbursed under Schwab's guarantee against unauthorized account activity.

Covered reliance on market makers, dealers, exchanges, clearing houses and other intermediaries to execute and settle client orders, the significant revenue from their order execution and securities lending payments, and the client dissatisfaction and damage claims if they fail to perform.
